title: Mechanisms of treatment-resistant depression
bottleneck: Roughly a third of depressed patients fail multiple adequate antidepressant trials, yet treatment-resistant depression has no agreed biological definition: it is defined by what did not work, not by a mechanism. Candidate mechanisms (glutamate dysfunction, inflammation, anhedonia circuits, HPA axis) are studied in isolation without a unifying framework.
why_it_blocks: Without mechanistic subtypes, treatment is trial-and-error across drug classes, condemning patients to months of ineffective therapy while suicide risk and functional loss accumulate.
current_state: Esketamine is approved for treatment-resistant depression with rapid but often transient effect. Research into inflammatory, metabolic, and circuit-based subtypes is active but has not produced a clinical test. Inflammatory and metabolic subtypes of depression are emerging as distinct entities, yet no clinic can currently test which subtype a patient has, keeping treatment selection empirical.
